title: Nanoscale Compositional Analysis of NiSix with Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy (EELS)
content: Nickel silicide (NiSix) has become an important material in the semi­conductor industry [1, 2]. It is formed through silicidation process, which involves a thin nickel film reacting with a silicon substrate at high temperatures. The most common species of NiSix include NiSi, Ni2Si, and NiSi2 [3]. NiSi is desirable as contact materials in electronic devices due to its low resistivity, high thermal stability, and compatibility [4]. The silicidation requires precise control as inappropriate processes can form unexpected Ni2Si and NiSi2 degrading the contact efficiency.
